verdict.rationale: Luma's Ray page documents transferring cinematic camera moves from a source video to new scenes, so a creator can dictate camera motion rather than accept the model's choice. Multi-Keyframe adds beat-by-beat control over what changes and what holds. However, no named camera-move controls (pan, zoom, orbit, static lock) or prompt-level camera directives are documented. missing for 10: explicit pan/zoom/orbit/static camera controls, documentation of how camera direction works without a reference video, hands-on corroboration that camera direction is followed.

support.subject: As a creator, I can direct camera moves (pan, zoom, orbit, static) instead of accepting whatever motion the model picks

citations.quote: Transfer cinematic camera moves across scenes, worlds, and styles.
Direct what changes and what holds, beat by beat. Sequence-level control, exposed at the API.
